claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child. I'm asking about my son Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Now I need to ask you:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. But I do help out financially - I give money towards his clothes, school things, and what he needs. I contribute regularly to help with his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility properly, I need to know:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or in lump sums)?**

This is important because to qualify for Child Benefit when you don't live with your child, you need to contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £26.05 per week towards Alex's upkeep - I make these payments weekly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail. I have a few more questions to ensure I have a complete picture:

**Does Alex currently live with someone else (for example, your ex-partner, a relative, or friend), and if so, is that person currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with my ex-partner, but they're not claiming Child Benefit for him - nobody else is getting it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Just a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, in care, or living in residential accommodation for an extended period?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. Alex is just living normally with my ex - he's not in hospital, care, or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year?**

(This won't affect your eligibility to receive Child Benefit, but it may mean you'd need to pay a tax charge on it.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into the income details right now - I'm mainly just trying to figure out if I'm actually eligible to claim it in the first place.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's absolutely fine - I have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review your situation:

- You have a son, Alex, who is 8 years old
- You live in the UK
- Alex lives with your ex-partner
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You contribute £26.05 per week towards Alex's upkeep
- Alex is not in hospital, care, or residential accommodation

Based on the rules, you can qualify for Child Benefit even when your child doesn't live with you, as long as you're contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their upkeep. The current Child Benefit rate for one child is £25.60 per week, and you're contributing £26.05 per week, which meets this requirement.

Since nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, you are eligible to claim it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

You meet all the requirements because you're contributing more than the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's upkeep, and nobody else is claiming for him. You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit.

If you have any other questions about the process, feel free to ask!
